Performers
Robert Casadesus (piano) Documented

The solo pianist is identified on the carrier, repository record and official discography. No other performer is claimed.

[2] [1] [4]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The original work is for solo piano. The particular performing edition used by Casadesus is not identified; the viewed Durand score is study evidence, not evidence that this exact copy or impression was used. Section boundaries are score-informed passage estimates, not bar alignments.

[7] [1] [2]
Recorded
1950-04-11 Documented

The official discography identifies 11 April 1950 for Children’s Corner and includes ML 4366 in the issue list. The LP’s 1951 publication and the 2022 transfer are separate dates.

[4]
Place
Columbia 30th Street Studio, New York, United States Documented

Venue and city are stated in the dated suite row; they are not inferred from the record company’s location.

[4]
Label
Columbia Masterworks Documented

The transferred carrier is a 12-inch vinyl LP; Debussy is on its second side.

[2] [1] [3]
Catalogue
ML 4366 (sleeve and library catalogue); ML 54366 (scanned disc label) Documented

Both forms occur in the evidence. The library dates the ML 4366 issue to 1951; the exact pressing date of the scanned ML 54366-labelled copy is not established. No explanation for the number variation is invented.

[2] [1] [3]
Matrix, take, sides
XLP 2933; disc 1, side 2, band 3 of 6 Documented

The side matrix is printed on the Debussy label. Individual session take and stamper identifiers are not established; the side matrix is not presented as a session take number.

[2] [5]
Transfer
Internet Archive Documented

The explicit ripping_operator credit is used. The separate catalogue/scanning operator and uploader are not substituted for the audio transfer operator.

[1]
Transfer date
2022-03-21 Documented

Item ripping_date is 20220321012946. This is the transfer date, not the 1950 session, 1951 LP issue, scan date or repository added date.

[1]
Processing
Technics SL1200MK5 turntable + Audio-⁠Technica AT95e cartridge → Radio Design Labs EZ-PH1 phono preamp → Focusrite Scarlett 2i2; Internet Archive VBR MP3 access derivative Documented

The stated lineage and digital formats are documented. The source-side file records SoX processing, but detailed settings, restoration, noise reduction, pitch correction and edits are not established. No such treatment is inferred from the sound or carrier-condition grade.

[1] [6]
Composition rights
Underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Debussy died in 1918 and the suite was published in 1908. This is territorial term reasoning for the composition, not worldwide clearance or a claim about an unidentified modern edition.

[3] [8] [10]
Recording rights
Rule 3 — EU public-domain term basis for a phonogram published before 1963; territorial, not worldwide. Documented

The documented LP issue is dated 1951, establishing publication before 1963 independently of the 1950 session. Its earlier 50-year phonogram term had expired before the 1 November 2013 extension threshold. US sound-recording status is not established. No Creative Commons licence or worldwide public-domain dedication is claimed.

[3] [1] [10] [11]

Claude Debussy, Children’s Corner, III. Serenade for the Doll; Robert Casadesus, piano. Recorded 11 April 1950, Columbia 30th Street Studio, New York; Columbia Masterworks ML 4366 issue dated 1951 (scanned label ML 54366), side 2, band 3. Internet Archive LP transfer, 21 March 2022. Rule 3 territorial EU basis; US status not established.

  1. Internet Archive — Columbia Children’s Corner / Forest Scenes — Item metadata: pianist, Columbia Masterworks, catalogue numbers ML 4366 and ML 54366, publication date 1951, transfer lineage, ripping operator and ripping date. Repository scan, public and added dates are kept separate from the session.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  2. Columbia — original LP sleeve and labels — Viewed four-page carrier scan. The Debussy label on PDF p. 4 reads ML 54366 and XLP 2933 and lists all six bands; sleeve identifies ML 4366. The two catalogue forms are retained without guessing why they differ.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. CiNii Books — Columbia ML 4366 — Columbia, c1951; Masterworks label; Robert Casadesus, piano; recording data undescribed. This is LP publication evidence, not session dating. Contributor authority gives Debussy’s dates as 1862–⁠1918.. Accessed 2026-10-18.
  4. Robert Casadesus — official discography — Children’s Corner row dated 1950-04-11: New York, Columbia 30th Street Studio, Robert Casadesus; lists Columbia ML 4366, X 355 and SL 222 among issues. The matching suite and catalogue establish the session independently of the LP’s 1951 publication.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Internet Archive — LP side and band metadata — One 12-inch 33⅓-rpm disc; Debussy occupies disc 1, side 2, bands 1–⁠6. The six selected files are these bands, not the Schumann side.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Internet Archive — LP digital file provenance — Selected disc1/02.01–⁠02.06 MP3 files and source side-level 24-bit FLAC derivatives. File metadata records VBR MP3 access copies and SoX processing of the side source; it does not document noise reduction or a modern remaster.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Debussy — Children’s Corner, Durand piano score — Movement studied on printed pp. 10–⁠15 (PDF pp. 12–⁠17). Viewed all musical pages, printed pp. 1–⁠28 (PDF pp. 3–⁠30), dedication and contents on PDF p. 2. Plate D. & F. 7188; 1908 copyright. The final page reads Février 1952: this is a later impression of the historical engraving, not a claim that the physical copy was printed in 1908.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. IMSLP — Children’s Corner, CD 119 (L. 113) — Work information: catalogue numbers, six movements, 1906–⁠08 composition and 1908 Durand publication. The catalogue’s premiere date is not used because it has not been independently reconciled with other accounts.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Morris Hastings — original Columbia programme note — Original LP sleeve note, also viewed in the carrier scan. Jimbo is described as a felt toy elephant. That image is attributed to the note; the sleeve’s unsupported tune-origin story and biographical details are not adopted.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  10. Directive 2006/116/EC — copyright and related-rights terms — Articles 1, 3 and 8: ordinary composition term and pre-extension phonogram terms and calendar calculation. Territorial term reasoning, not a licence.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  11. Directive 2011/77/EU — phonogram term extension — Article 1(3), inserting Article 10(5): the extended terms concern recordings still protected on 1 November 2013; Article 2 gives the implementation date. Earlier expired terms are not revived by this rule.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
